intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the iconic 14th-century Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok robe. Many rental shops surrounding the palace offer affordable Hanbok rentals, and wearing one grants you free entry to the palace. Witness the ceremonial Changing of the Royal Guard and stroll through the grand courtyards for an immersive dive into Joseon Dynasty culture.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional market, famous for its vibrant food stalls. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (mini seaweed rice rolls), tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with local vendors and experience the authentic sights, sounds, and flavors of everyday Korean culinary life.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Dance Class
experiences.description: Learn choreography from your favorite K-Pop songs at one of Hongdae's many dedicated K-Pop dance academies. Professional instructors teach routines from groups like BTS, BLACKPINK, and NewJeans in a fun, energetic group setting. This is a quintessential K-culture experience that lets you live out your idol fantasies and connect with fellow K-Pop fans from around the world.

experiences.name: Insadong Cultural Village & Tea House Exploration
experiences.description: Wander through the charming alleyways of Insadong, Seoul's premier cultural district filled with traditional tea houses, antique shops, indie galleries, and Korean craft stores. Stop into a traditional Hanok-style tea house to enjoy a ceremonial cup of omija (five-flavor berry) or barley tea paired with Korean rice cakes. Explore Ssamziegil, a quirky open-air shopping complex showcasing local artisan goods and handmade crafts.

experiences.name: Authentic Korean BBQ Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Enjoy a classic Korean BBQ dinner at one of Mapo-gu's legendary charcoal grill restaurants, famous for their premium samgyeopsal (pork belly) and galbi (beef short ribs). Grill your own meat tableside, wrap it in fresh perilla leaves and lettuce, and pair it with an array of banchan (side dishes) and a glass of soju or makgeolli. This communal dining ritual is central to Korean social culture and an unmissable culinary highlight.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, then take the Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or bus to Bupyeong station. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Pick up a T-money card at the airport convenience store for easy transit use throughout the trip.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack at a 24-hour GS25 or CU convenience store near the hotel — try triangle kimbap, instant ramen, or hotteok (₩1,000–3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you'll be tired from the flight. Buy your T-money card at the airport (₩4,000 deposit). Exchange some cash at the airport for better rates. Dress warmly; December temperatures hover around 3°C.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. Enjoy the complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn if included. Explore the Bupyeong area on foot — visit Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center (Bupyeong Modoo Mall), one of Korea's largest underground malls, great for affordable K-fashion and accessories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway (Line 1) to Incheon Chinatown — Korea's only Chinatown, just 2 stops away. Walk through the colorful murals and archways, then head to nearby Jayu Park (Freedom Park) for panoramic views of Incheon port. Explore the Open Port Area with its historic Japanese and Chinese colonial architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Sinpo International Market (신포국제시장) in Incheon for street food and local eats. Try the famous Sinpo dak-gangjeong (sweet crispy chicken) and browse the stalls.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store (₩2,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) at a Chinatown restaurant — authentic and cheap (₩6,000–8,000)
meals.dinner: Sinpo Market street food: dak-gangjeong, tteokbokki, sundae (₩5,000–8,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: All locations today are within Incheon and easily reachable by subway from Bupyeong. Wear layers — it will be cold. Sinpo Market is lively in the evening despite winter.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway from Bupyeong to Hongdae (Line 1 to Seoul, transfer to Line 2 — about 50 min, ₩1,500). Explore Hongdae's vibrant street art, indie shops, and K-culture scene. Visit the Hongdae Free Market area and browse affordable K-pop merchandise shops and vintage clothing stores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area for more affordable shopping and street food. Then head to Gyeongui Line Forest Park (경의선숲길), a beautiful linear park perfect for a winter stroll. Visit the Yonsei University campus nearby for a classic Korean university atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Hongdae for the evening — the area comes alive at night with buskers, street performers, and K-culture energy. Visit a norebang (karaoke room) for a quintessential Korean experience (₩10,000–15,000/hour per room).

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (₩2,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Tteokbokki and eomuk (fish cake) from Hongdae street stalls (₩4,000–6,000)
meals.dinner: Budae jjigae (army stew) at a local Sinchon restaurant — hearty and warming for winter (₩8,000–10,000)

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae is the heart of K-culture and youth culture in Seoul. Keep an eye out for idol fan cafes and K-pop pop-up stores. Subway fare from Bupyeong to Hongdae is approximately ₩1,500 each way.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Gyeongbokgung Palace (경복궁) — Seoul's grandest Joseon-era palace. Rent a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) from one of the many rental shops near the palace entrance (₩10,000–15,000/2 hours) and get free entry to the palace while wearing it. Explore the palace grounds and Gyeonghoeru Pavilion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Bukchon Hanok Village (북촌한옥마을) — a stunning neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Stroll the narrow alleys and enjoy the contrast of old and new Seoul. Then visit Insadong (인사동) for traditional crafts, tea houses, and K-culture souvenirs at reasonable prices.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong's Ssamziegil courtyard complex for indie shops and street food. Head to nearby Tapgol Park area for a quiet evening walk.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (₩2,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Gimbap and doenjang jjigae at a local bunsik restaurant near Insadong (₩5,000–7,000)
meals.dinner: Samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) at a budget BBQ restaurant in Insadong or Jongno area — look for set menus (₩10,000–13,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung Palace entry is ₩3,000 (free with hanbok). The palace is stunning in winter — check if there are special winter light events. Bukchon can be slippery in cold weather, so wear good shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gwangjang Market (광장시장) — one of Seoul's oldest and most famous traditional markets. This is a must for local food lovers. Try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini kimbap), and yukhoe (beef tartare) for breakfast/brunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a futuristic landmark designed by Zaha Hadid. Explore the free outdoor areas and any free exhibitions inside. Then visit Dongdaemun History & Culture Park for a glimpse of Seoul's ancient city walls.
day_by_day.evening: Dongdaemun is famous for its massive shopping malls that open late into the night. Browse Doota Mall, Migliore, or the outdoor Dongdaemun Market for affordable K-fashion. The area is especially lively on weekends.

meals.breakfast: Gwangjang Market — bindaetteok and mayak gimbap (₩5,000–8,000)
meals.lunch: More Gwangjang Market food or a nearby kalguksu (knife noodle) restaurant (₩7,000–9,000)
meals.dinner: Street food around Dongdaemun — tteokbokki, hotteok, and eomuk (₩5,000–7,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is busiest on weekends — arrive early to beat the crowds. DDP often hosts free cultural events and exhibitions. Dongdaemun shopping malls stay open until 5 AM — great for night owls.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Myeongdong (명동) — Seoul's most famous shopping and beauty district. Browse the countless K-beauty shops (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young) for affordable skincare and cosmetics. Many shops offer free samples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up to Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower) via the free cable car or hiking trail. Enjoy panoramic views of Seoul in winter. Visit the famous love lock fence. Then explore the surrounding Namsan Park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Myeongdong for the famous street food market that sets up in the evening. This is one of the best street food experiences in Seoul. Try Korean corn dogs, tteokbokki, and hotteok.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (₩2,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Myeongdong Kyoja — famous for kalguksu and mandu dumplings, a Seoul institution (₩9,000–11,000)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food market — try 3–4 different items (₩8,000–12,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower cable car costs ₩9,000 round trip; the observation deck costs extra (₩16,000) but the views from the park are free. Myeongdong street food vendors typically set up around 5–6 PM. Olive Young is the best place for affordable K-beauty products.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace (창덕궁) and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). The Secret Garden requires a guided tour (₩8,000) and is especially beautiful in winter with snow-dusted pavilions. Book in advance or arrive early as spots are limited.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ikseon-dong Hanok Village (익선동) — a trendy neighborhood of converted hanok houses turned into cafes, restaurants, and boutiques. More authentic and less touristy than Bukchon. Perfect for K-culture exploration and Instagram-worthy spots.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Jongno 3-ga area for pojangmacha (street tent bars) — a classic Korean evening experience. Sit under a tent, order anju (bar snacks) like pajeon (green onion pancake) and makgeolli (rice wine) for a very local, budget-friendly evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (₩2,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong cafe lunch — many offer affordable set menus or Korean fusion dishes (₩8,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Pojangmacha in Jongno — makgeolli + pajeon + sundae (₩10,000–15,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Palace entry is ₩3,000; Secret Garden tour is ₩8,000 extra. Book the Secret Garden tour online in advance at the palace website. Ikseon-dong is very photogenic — great for K-culture content.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Itaewon and walk up to Haebangchon (HBC) — a multicultural neighborhood with a local, non-touristy vibe. Explore the hillside streets and independent cafes. Then visit the nearby Bogwangdong neighborhood for a glimpse of authentic Seoul residential life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Yongsan Electronics Market (용산전자상가) — one of Asia's largest electronics markets. Great for browsing K-tech, gaming gear, and electronics at competitive prices. Even if you don't buy, it's a fascinating cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Visit War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관) — free entry and one of Seoul's most impressive museums covering Korean history and the Korean War. The outdoor exhibits are accessible even in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (₩2,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Haebangchon local restaurant — try dosirak (Korean lunch box set) or kimchi jjigae (₩7,000–9,000)
meals.dinner: Yongsan area — galbi-tang (short rib soup) at a local restaurant, warming for winter (₩9,000–12,000)

day_by_day.notes: War Memorial of Korea is free and open Tuesday–Sunday, 9:30 AM–6 PM. Yongsan Electronics Market is a great place to buy affordable Korean tech accessories. Haebangchon has a great mix of Korean and international culture.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World (롯데월드) in Jamsil — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks. Budget option: buy a day pass (₩54,000) or just explore the free Lotte World Mall and Magic Island outdoor area. Alternatively, visit the free Lotte World Folk Museum inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Seokchon Lake (석촌호수) adjacent to Lotte World — a beautiful lake park that's lovely even in winter. Then explore the Jamsil area and visit the COEX Mall underground shopping complex nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gangnam (강남) for the evening — explore Garosu-gil (가로수길), a tree-lined street with boutiques, cafes, and restaurants. Window shop and enjoy the upscale but walkable neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (₩2,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: COEX Mall food court — wide variety of Korean dishes at reasonable prices (₩8,000–10,000)
meals.dinner: Garosu-gil area — look for affordable Korean set meal restaurants or a cozy ramen shop (₩8,000–12,000)

day_by_day.notes: If skipping Lotte World rides, the mall and lake area are completely free. COEX Mall also has a famous underground library (Starfield Library) — free to visit and very photogenic. Gangnam subway station is on Line 2.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (조계사) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, located in central Seoul. Free entry. The temple is beautifully decorated with lanterns year-round and may have special winter decorations. A peaceful contrast to the busy city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) — an elevated highway converted into a beautiful urban stream. Walk along the stream from Gwanghwamun toward Dongdaemun. In winter, there are often special light installations along the stream.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major celebration! Head to Myeongdong or Hongdae for the festive atmosphere — streets are decorated, carolers perform, and the city feels magical. Many young Koreans celebrate Christmas Eve as a romantic holiday.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (₩2,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Cheonggyecheon area — try a local gukbap (rice soup) restaurant for a warming winter meal (₩7,000–9,000)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special — treat yourself to Korean fried chicken and beer (chimaek) at a local chicken restaurant in Myeongdong or Hongdae (₩15,000–20,000)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the busiest nights in Seoul — expect crowds in Myeongdong and Hongdae. Cheonggyecheon Stream often has a special winter light festival (Lantern Festival) — check current events. Jogyesa Temple is free and open daily.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (경희궁) — a lesser-known but beautiful palace that's free to enter and usually uncrowded. Then walk to the Seoul Museum of History (서울역사박물관) next door — also free and excellent for understanding Seoul's history and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Seodaemun Prison History Hall (서대문형무소역사관) — a powerful museum in a former Japanese colonial-era prison, important for understanding Korean independence history (₩3,000 entry). Then explore the surrounding Seodaemun area.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Noryangjin Fish Market (노량진수산시장) — one of Seoul's largest wholesale fish markets. Buy fresh seafood at the market stalls and have it prepared at the restaurants upstairs for a fraction of restaurant prices. A unique and memorable experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (₩2,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Near Seodaemun — sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) at a local restaurant, perfect for cold weather (₩7,000–9,000)
meals.dinner: Noryangjin Fish Market — buy fresh sashimi, crab, or shrimp and have it prepared upstairs (₩15,000–25,000 depending on selection)

day_by_day.notes: Many attractions are open on Christmas Day in Korea as it's a public holiday but celebrated differently than in the West. Noryangjin Fish Market is open 24 hours — the freshest seafood is in the early morning, but evening is fine too. Seodaemun Prison is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (수원화성) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1 hour from Bupyeong by subway. The fortress walls stretch 5.7 km and offer great winter walks with views of the city. Entry is ₩1,000.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Paldalmun Gate area and the traditional market nearby. Visit the Hwaseong Haenggung Palace (행궁) — the temporary palace used by King Jeongjo (₩1,500 entry). Walk the fortress walls for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong/Incheon area. Spend your last full evening exploring the Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center for any last-minute souvenir shopping. Have a farewell Korean BBQ dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (₩2,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Suwon galbi (Suwon-style short ribs) — Suwon is famous for this dish; look for affordable lunch sets near the fortress (₩10,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: Korean BBQ near Bupyeong hotel — samgyeopsal or chadolbaegi (beef brisket) farewell dinner (₩12,000–15,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong is easily reached from Bupyeong via subway (Line 1 to Suwon Station, about 45–60 min, ₩1,800). The fortress is beautiful in winter and rarely crowded. Suwon galbi is a regional specialty not to be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — pack and check out of Toyoko Inn. If time allows, grab a last Korean breakfast at a nearby bunsik restaurant: haejang-guk (hangover soup) or kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout rice soup) — a classic Korean morning meal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Incheon International Airport via AREX or airport bus from Bupyeong. Allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute Korean snacks, cosmetics, or gifts (Choco Pie, Pepero, Korean seaweed, etc.).
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Local bunsik restaurant near hotel — haejang-guk or gimbap (₩5,000–8,000)
meals.lunch: Airport food court or convenience store (₩8,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: On the plane or airport restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Bupyeong to Incheon Airport takes approximately 40–60 minutes by AREX or bus. Keep your T-money card topped up for the airport journey. Pack any liquid K-beauty products in checked luggage. Korean duty-free snacks make great affordable gifts — Choco Pie multipacks, dried seaweed, and instant ramyeon are popular choices.

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect baggage, then take the Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or a limousine bus to Bupyeong station area. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong and settle into your room.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a 24-hour convenience store (GS25 or CU) near the hotel — try triangle kimbap, instant ramen, or hotteok for a quick, affordable bite after arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Dress warmly — December temperatures average around 3°C. Pick up a T-money card at the airport convenience store or ticket machine for easy transit use throughout the trip. Exchange some cash (KRW) at the airport for better rates. Rest well tonight as Day 2 begins your full exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Start your first full day with a walk around Bupyeong Modoo Mall and Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center, one of Korea's largest underground markets. Browse K-fashion, accessories, and local goods. Get a feel for everyday Korean shopping culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway (Line 1) from Bupyeong to Incheon Chinatown and Sinpo International Market. Explore the colorful murals, Chinese-Korean fusion architecture, and the nearby Jayu Park — Korea's first Western-style park with great views of the port. Walk along the Open Port Area to see colonial-era buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Sinpo International Market for evening street food. The market is famous for Sinpo-style dakgangjeong (sweet crispy fried chicken). Stroll the lit-up market stalls before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby bakery like Paris Baguette — try a warm pastry and coffee (around 5,000–8,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) or tangsuyuk (sweet and sour pork) at one of the authentic Chinese-Korean restaurants in Incheon Chinatown (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Sinpo dakgangjeong and tteokbokki at Sinpo International Market stalls (8,000–12,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Wear layers and a warm coat. The underground shopping center is a great way to stay warm while exploring. Bupyeong and Incheon Chinatown are easily connected by subway Line 1 — about 10 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Bupyeong to central Seoul via subway (Line 1 to Seoul Station, approx. 40–50 min). Head to Gyeongbokgung Palace, the grandest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces. Catch the 10:00 AM Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at the main gate. Rent a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) from a nearby rental shop to enter the palace for free and take stunning photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Bukchon Hanok Village, a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Wander the narrow alleys, enjoy the contrast of old architecture against the modern city skyline, and visit small craft shops and galleries. Continue to Insadong for a leisurely afternoon browsing antique shops, tea houses, and K-culture souvenir stores.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong's Ssamziegil — an open-air courtyard mall with indie shops, art installations, and street food. Enjoy the festive December atmosphere with holiday lights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store onigiri and coffee before departing.
meals.lunch: Traditional Korean set meal (한정식 hanjeongsik lite) near Gyeongbokgung — try bibimbap or doenjang jjigae at a local restaurant (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a cozy restaurant in Insadong — try samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) at a mid-range BBQ spot (15,000–20,000 KRW per person).

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays. Hanbok rental shops near the palace charge around 10,000–20,000 KRW for 2 hours. Bukchon Hanok Village asks visitors to be quiet out of respect for residents. Carry hand warmers — it will be cold walking outdoors.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Namsan Mountain and N Seoul Tower. Take the Namsan Cable Car up for panoramic winter views of Seoul. Visit the famous love lock fence and enjoy the crisp morning air. The tower area is magical in December with holiday decorations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and make your way to Myeongdong, Seoul's most famous shopping and beauty district. Explore K-beauty stores (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young), fashion boutiques, and the lively street food scene. This is the heart of Korean pop culture commerce.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Myeongdong for the evening street food experience — one of the best in Seoul. The street vendors light up at night and the energy is electric even in winter.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast near the hotel or at a café in Myeongdong before heading to Namsan.
meals.lunch: Street food lunch in Myeongdong — try hotteok (sweet pancake), eomuk (fish cake skewers), and gyeran-ppang (egg bread) from vendors (5,000–10,000 KRW total).
meals.dinner: Sit-down dinner at a Myeongdong restaurant — try naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles) or galbitang (short rib soup) to warm up (12,000–18,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower admission is around 21,000 KRW for adults. The cable car costs about 9,500 KRW round trip. Myeongdong is extremely popular — expect crowds on Friday evening. Olive Young is a must-visit for K-beauty products at reasonable prices.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). This UNESCO World Heritage Site is one of Seoul's most beautiful palaces, especially with winter frost on the traditional architecture. Book the Secret Garden tour in advance (guided tours only, limited spots).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Changgyeonggung Palace or head to the Jongno area to explore Tapgol Park and the traditional Jongno street. Visit Jogyesa Temple, the head temple of Korean Buddhism, beautifully decorated with lanterns for the winter season.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream for a romantic evening walk along the illuminated waterway. The stream is lit up beautifully in winter and is a peaceful escape from the busy city streets.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean breakfast at a local sikdang (식당) near the hotel — try haejang-guk (hangover soup) or congee (juk) (8,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Lunch near Changdeokgung — try a warm sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) at a local restaurant (9,000–13,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Dinner in the Jongno area — try dakhanmari (whole chicken in broth) at the famous Dakhanmari Alley near Dongdaemun (15,000–20,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours must be booked online in advance at the palace website. Tours are available in English. Wear very warm shoes as you'll be walking on stone paths. Cheonggyecheon Stream is free to visit and accessible from multiple subway stations.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — Zaha Hadid's iconic futuristic building. Visit the design exhibitions and the surrounding Dongdaemun History & Culture Park. The area is fascinating for its blend of ancient city wall ruins and ultra-modern architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gwangjang Market, one of Seoul's oldest and most authentic traditional markets. This is a paradise for local food lovers — browse the fabric stalls and food hall packed with grandmothers cooking traditional dishes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Dongdaemun for the famous night shopping experience. Dongdaemun's fashion malls (Doota, Migliore) open late and are buzzing on Sunday evenings. Browse K-fashion at wholesale and retail prices.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near the hotel — try a Korean-style egg sandwich and Americano at a local café (6,000–9,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Iconic lunch at Gwangjang Market — must-try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap (addictive mini kimbap), and yukhoe (beef tartare). Budget around 10,000–15,000 KRW.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a restaurant near Dongdaemun — try gopchang (grilled intestines) or a hearty Korean stew (13,000–18,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: DDP admission varies by exhibition — check the website for current shows. Gwangjang Market is busiest at lunch and is a must for authentic Korean food culture. Dongdaemun shopping malls are open until 4–5 AM, so no rush in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress, a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1 hour from Bupyeong by subway. Walk along the impressive 5.7 km fortress walls that encircle the old city. The winter scenery with frost on the stone walls is stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Haenggung Palace (Hwaseong Haenggung) inside the fortress grounds. Visit the Suwon Traditional Culture Center to learn about local crafts and history. Browse the traditional market street near the fortress.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong/Incheon area. Spend a relaxed evening near the hotel, exploring the local Bupyeong neighborhood — visit a jjimjilbang (Korean sauna/bathhouse) for a warm, relaxing evening experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store before departing for Suwon.
meals.lunch: Suwon galbi (Suwon-style short ribs) — the city's most famous dish — at a local restaurant near the fortress (15,000–25,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Jjimjilbang restaurant or a nearby Korean restaurant in Bupyeong — try kimchi jjigae or budae jjigae (army stew) (10,000–15,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress admission is around 1,000 KRW. Take subway Line 1 from Bupyeong directly to Suwon Station (about 50 minutes). A jjimjilbang entry costs around 10,000–15,000 KRW and includes access to hot baths, saunas, and rest areas — perfect for warming up after a cold day.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Hongdae (Hongik University area) — the epicenter of Korean youth culture, indie music, and street art. Explore the vibrant murals, quirky cafés, and K-pop culture shops. Visit the Trick Eye Museum or LINE Friends Store for fun K-culture experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area. The Ewha campus is architecturally stunning with its famous underground ECC building. Browse the trendy shops and cafés in Sinchon, popular with university students.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the evening — the neighborhood truly comes alive at night with buskers, live music, and street performances. Visit a norebang (karaoke room) for an authentic K-culture experience.

meals.breakfast: Trendy café breakfast in Hongdae — try a Korean-style brunch at one of the many Instagram-worthy cafés (8,000–13,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Hongdae — try tteokbokki and sundae (blood sausage) at a pojangmacha (street tent) or a casual restaurant (8,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Hongdae restaurant — try yangnyeom chicken (Korean fried chicken) with a cold Hite beer at a local chimaek spot (15,000–20,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Norebang rooms cost around 15,000–25,000 KRW per hour for a private room. Hongdae is very lively on weekday evenings — expect street performers even in December. The Trick Eye Museum costs around 15,000 KRW. Hongdae is accessible via subway Line 2 or the AREX airport line.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Itaewon and the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — one of Korea's finest private art museums featuring both traditional Korean art and contemporary international works. The building itself, designed by three world-renowned architects, is a masterpiece.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Itaewon's multicultural neighborhood — browse the international restaurants, vintage clothing shops, and antique stores on Antique Furniture Street. Walk up to Haebangchon (HBC) for a more local, artsy vibe with independent cafés and boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gangnam district for the evening. Visit COEX Mall — one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls — and the famous COEX Starfield Library, a stunning public library inside the mall. Browse the bookstore and enjoy the festive Christmas decorations.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast near the hotel before heading out — try a warm bowl of seolleongtang (ox bone soup) at a local restaurant (9,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: International lunch in Itaewon — try a Korean-Mexican fusion burrito or a Middle Eastern shawarma for a multicultural experience (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Dinner in Gangnam — try a modern Korean restaurant or a trendy ramen shop near COEX (13,000–20,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Leeum Museum admission is around 10,000 KRW. COEX Starfield Library is free to visit and is one of Seoul's most photogenic spots. Gangnam is accessible via subway Line 2. The area will be beautifully decorated for Christmas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park for a morning winter hike. The mountain park sits within Seoul city limits and offers spectacular views of the snow-dusted peaks and the city below. Choose a beginner-friendly trail like the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and head to Myeongdong Cathedral — Seoul's most iconic Catholic church, beautifully lit for Christmas Eve. The area around the cathedral will be festively decorated. Browse the Christmas markets and enjoy the holiday atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Christmas Eve in Seoul — the city goes all out with lights and celebrations. Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream or City Hall Plaza for the Christmas light festival. Many young Koreans celebrate Christmas Eve like Valentine's Day, making the city especially lively.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the hike — convenience store kimbap and hot coffee or a quick meal near the hotel.
meals.lunch: Post-hike warm meal near Bukhansan — try a hearty doenjang jjigae or kimchi jjigae at a mountain restaurant (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner — treat yourself to a Korean BBQ restaurant in Myeongdong or a nice Korean fusion restaurant (20,000–30,000 KRW per person).

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan National Park is free to enter. Wear proper hiking boots and warm layers — trails can be icy in December. Bring crampons or ice grips for shoes if possible. Christmas Eve in Seoul is very romantic and festive — the city is beautifully illuminated. Book dinner in advance if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (less crowded than Gyeongbokgung) and the Seoul Museum of History next door. Learn about Seoul's transformation from ancient Joseon capital to modern megacity through fascinating exhibits. The museum is free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a charming neighborhood of traditional hanok houses converted into cafés, art galleries, and boutiques. This is a quieter, more authentic alternative to Bukchon. Visit the Yun Dong-ju Literary Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Lotte World Tower in Jamsil for the evening. Visit the Sky Observatory on the 117th–123rd floors for breathtaking nighttime views of Seoul. The tower and surrounding Lotte World Mall are spectacularly lit for Christmas.

meals.breakfast: Christmas morning café breakfast — try a festive holiday drink and pastry at a cozy Seochon café (8,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Seochon Village — try a traditional Korean meal at a hanok café-restaurant (12,000–18,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner near Lotte World — try a nice Korean or international restaurant in the Jamsil area (20,000–30,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Seoul Museum of History is free. Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory costs around 27,000 KRW. Many restaurants may have special Christmas menus — check in advance. Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea, so some smaller shops may be closed but major attractions remain open.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of the largest museums in Asia, with an incredible collection of Korean artifacts spanning thousands of years. The museum is free and takes 2–3 hours to explore properly. Don't miss the Goryeo celadon and Joseon white porcelain collections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the War Memorial of Korea nearby — a powerful and moving museum documenting Korea's military history, including the Korean War. The outdoor exhibits with tanks, aircraft, and warships are impressive even in winter. Free admission.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your last full evening in the Yongsan Electronics Market or head back to a favorite neighborhood for final shopping and souvenir hunting. Visit a traditional Korean tea house for a warm, reflective end to your trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery near the hotel for a relaxed morning start.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the National Museum of Korea's cafeteria or a nearby restaurant — try a Korean set meal (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a memorable Korean meal. Try a traditional Korean royal cuisine restaurant or a premium Korean BBQ spot (25,000–35,000 KRW per person).

day_by_day.notes: Both the National Museum of Korea and the War Memorial are free. The National Museum is closed on Mondays. Allow at least 2 hours for each museum. This is a great day for reflection on Korean history and culture before your trip ends. Pack souvenirs tonight to prepare for departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — take a leisurely walk around the Bupyeong neighborhood. Visit a local juk (porridge) restaurant for a light, healthy Korean breakfast. Do any last-minute shopping at Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center for affordable K-fashion and accessories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, visit a nearby café for a final Korean coffee experience. Pack and check out of the hotel. Head to Incheon International Airport via AREX or limousine bus (allow 60–90 minutes from Bupyeong). Use remaining KRW at the airport duty-free shops.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Incheon International Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of K-culture, incredible food, and unforgettable experiences in Seoul and Incheon.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — try juk (rice porridge) with various toppings at a local porridge restaurant (8,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport — try a Korean meal at one of the many airport restaurants before departure (12,000–18,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: On the plane or at the airport depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at Toyoko Inn is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with the hotel. Incheon Airport is one of the world's best airports with excellent shopping, dining, and cultural experiences (free Korean cultural performances and craft workshops in the transit area). Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. T-money card can be refunded at the airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the iconic 14th-century Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok robe. Many rental shops surrounding the palace offer affordable Hanbok rentals, and wearing one grants you free entry to the palace. Witness the ceremonial Changing of the Royal Guard and stroll through the grand courtyards for an immersive dive into Joseon Dynasty culture.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional market, famous for its vibrant food stalls. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (mini seaweed rice rolls), tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with local vendors and experience the authentic sights, sounds, and flavors of everyday Korean culinary life.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Dance Class
experiences.description: Learn choreography from your favorite K-Pop songs at one of Hongdae's many dedicated K-Pop dance academies. Professional instructors teach routines from groups like BTS, BLACKPINK, and NewJeans in a fun, energetic group setting. This is a quintessential K-culture experience that lets you live out your idol fantasies and connect with fellow K-Pop fans from around the world.

experiences.name: Insadong Cultural Village & Tea House Exploration
experiences.description: Wander through the charming alleyways of Insadong, Seoul's premier cultural district filled with traditional tea houses, antique shops, indie galleries, and Korean craft stores. Stop into a traditional Hanok-style tea house to enjoy a ceremonial cup of omija (five-flavor berry) or barley tea paired with Korean rice cakes. Explore Ssamziegil, a quirky open-air shopping complex showcasing local artisan goods and handmade crafts.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 22:30 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight is late evening
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange private airport transfer to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Check in, freshen up, and settle into the hotel. Light late-night snack near the hotel if hungry.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store snack or 24-hour ramen shop near Bupyeong station (Bupyeong is known for its night food scene)

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at night — prioritize rest. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements in advance. Keep Day 2 morning light to recover from jet lag.

day_by_day.morning: Slow start to recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast, then take a short walk around Bupyeong district to get oriented. Visit Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center for a quick browse — one of Korea's largest underground malls, great for warming up on a cold December morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway from Bupyeong to explore Incheon's Chinatown and Jayu Park — a short, scenic introduction to Korean-Chinese culture. Walk along the colorful murals of Sinpo International Market and pick up local street snacks like hotteok (sweet pancakes) and tteokbokki to warm up.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Sinpo International Market area for dinner. Return to hotel early for a good night's rest before the full Seoul itinerary begins.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café
meals.lunch: Sinpo International Market street food — jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) at a traditional Incheon Chinatown restaurant such as Gonghwachun, one of Korea's oldest Chinese restaurants
meals.dinner: Premium Korean BBQ at a local Bupyeong restaurant — try Hanwoo (Korean beef) at a well-regarded local grill house near Bupyeong station

day_by_day.notes: This is an orientation day. Keep pace relaxed. Temperatures will be around 3°C — dress in warm layers. Bupyeong subway station (Line 1 & 7) is your main transit hub.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Bupyeong to central Seoul (approx. 50–60 min by subway). Begin with the Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience — arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat crowds. Rent a premium Hanbok from a nearby rental shop (Gyeongbokgung Hanbok rental shops open from 9:00 AM) and explore the stunning 14th-century palace grounds in traditional dress. Visit Gyeonghoeru Pavilion and the National Folk Museum of Korea within the palace complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Bukchon Hanok Village — a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Stroll the winding alleys, admire the architecture, and enjoy panoramic views of Seoul. Visit a premium tea house such as Cha Masineun Tteul for a warm traditional tea ceremony experience.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong Cultural Village for an evening wander through galleries, craft shops, and lantern-lit alleyways. Browse Ssamziegil courtyard for artisan goods and unique Korean souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a warm pastry and coffee at a café near Bupyeong station before departing
meals.lunch: Traditional Korean set meal (hanjeongsik) at Tosokchon Samgyetang near Gyeongbokgung — famous for its premium ginseng chicken soup, perfect for cold weather
meals.dinner: Upscale Korean cuisine at Jungsik or a premium restaurant in the Insadong/Anguk area — try a modern Korean tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays — Thursday is perfect. Hanbok rental is included in the experience. Wear thermal underlayers as you'll be outdoors most of the day in sub-zero wind chill.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Book the Secret Garden guided tour in advance (tours run at set times). The winter landscape of bare trees and frozen ponds is hauntingly beautiful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Insadong Cultural Village & Tea House Experience in depth — wander through traditional craft galleries, visit the Unhyeongung Royal Residence, and enjoy a premium tea ceremony at a historic tea house. Browse handmade ceramics, calligraphy, and Korean art.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to Myeongdong for evening shopping and street food. Visit Lotte Department Store or Shinsegae for premium Korean beauty and fashion brands. Enjoy the festive Christmas decorations throughout Myeongdong.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near Anguk station — try Café Bora for their signature purple latte and Korean-style pastries
meals.lunch: Premium bibimbap at Gogung restaurant in Insadong — known for their authentic Jeonju-style bibimbap served in a traditional setting
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja for premium handmade kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) and mandu (dumplings) — a Seoul institution, or upgrade to a nearby upscale Korean restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Book the Changdeokgung Secret Garden tour online in advance at the official palace website. The garden tour is approximately 90 minutes with a guide.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour — Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional market. Arrive in the morning when the market is at its most vibrant. Sample bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), yukhoe (Korean beef tartare), and freshly made tteok (rice cakes). A guided food tour provides cultural context and access to the best stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Cheonggyecheon Stream for a scenic winter walk along the illuminated waterway. Continue to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — Zaha Hadid's iconic futuristic building — for a design and culture exhibition. Browse the surrounding Dongdaemun fashion district.
day_by_day.afternoon_note: Saturday markets are especially lively — Gwangjang is best experienced on weekends
day_by_day.evening: Head to Namsan Seoul Tower for panoramic night views of the city. Take the cable car up and enjoy the glittering Seoul skyline. Attach a love lock on the fence as a travel memento.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast before heading to Gwangjang Market
meals.lunch: Full immersive street food experience at Gwangjang Market — this IS the lunch. Budget ₩30,000–50,000 for a thorough tasting tour
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at N.Grill, the revolving restaurant atop Namsan Seoul Tower — one of Seoul's most iconic fine dining experiences with panoramic city views

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is open daily but especially vibrant on Saturdays. Book N.Grill at Namsan Tower well in advance — it is a popular fine dining destination. Cable car tickets can be purchased on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul. Attend a morning ceremony if timing allows, and admire the beautiful winter lantern decorations. Walk through the surrounding Bukchon area for a peaceful Sunday morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a charming, less-touristy neighborhood with independent galleries, vintage cafés, and traditional hanok architecture. Visit the Yun Dong-ju Literary Museum and browse local art spaces.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to Gangnam district for an upscale evening. Visit COEX Mall and the famous COEX Starfield Library. Explore the Apgujeong Rodeo Street for premium Korean fashion and beauty boutiques.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at a premium café in Seochon Village — try Café Onion Anguk or a similar artisan café known for Korean-style pastries and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Traditional Korean temple food (사찰음식) at Balwoo Gongyang near Jogyesa Temple — a Michelin-recommended restaurant serving authentic Buddhist cuisine
meals.dinner: Premium Korean BBQ in Gangnam — Maple Tree House in Itaewon/Gangnam area for premium Hanwoo beef, or Gaon (three Michelin stars) for the ultimate Korean fine dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Gaon restaurant requires advance reservation and is one of Korea's most prestigious dining experiences. Seochon Village is quieter than Bukchon and offers a more authentic local atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Take the K-Pop Idol Dance Class in Hongdae — learn choreography from iconic K-Pop songs at one of Hongdae's dedicated dance academies (such as 1MILLION Dance Studio or similar). Classes typically run 1–2 hours and are led by professional instructors. Book in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hongdae neighborhood — Seoul's vibrant youth and arts district. Browse independent boutiques, K-Pop merchandise stores, and street art. Visit the Hongdae Free Market area (weekends are best, but the neighborhood is lively daily). Explore the nearby Yonsei University campus for architecture and café culture.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Hongdae for the evening entertainment scene. Catch a live busking performance (Hongdae is famous for street performances even in winter). Visit a premium cocktail bar or rooftop lounge in the area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before heading to Hongdae
meals.lunch: Trendy brunch or lunch at a popular Hongdae café-restaurant — try Anthracite Coffee Roasters for specialty coffee and light bites, followed by a meal at a well-regarded local restaurant
meals.dinner: Premium omakase sushi or modern Korean fusion at a Hongdae/Mapo area restaurant — the neighborhood has excellent upscale dining options alongside its street food culture

day_by_day.notes: Book the K-Pop dance class at least 3–5 days in advance as popular time slots fill quickly. Wear comfortable athletic clothing. 1MILLION Dance Studio is world-famous and offers tourist-friendly classes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums. Explore the permanent collection of Korean art, history, and artifacts spanning thousands of years. The museum is free to enter and world-class in quality.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Itaewon for a multicultural afternoon. Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — one of Korea's premier private art museums featuring both traditional Korean art and contemporary international works. Explore the surrounding Hannam-dong neighborhood, known for its upscale boutiques and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Itaewon's cosmopolitan dining and nightlife scene. The area offers Seoul's most diverse international restaurant options alongside premium Korean establishments.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near Bupyeong before departing
meals.lunch: Museum café at the National Museum of Korea, or a nearby restaurant in Yongsan — try a premium Korean set lunch
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Mingles in Hannam-dong — a two Michelin-starred restaurant blending Korean and international culinary techniques, one of Seoul's most celebrated restaurants

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is closed on Mondays — Tuesday is perfect. Leeum Museum may have temporary exhibitions; check their website for current shows. Mingles requires advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress — a UNESCO World Heritage Site just 30 minutes from Seoul by subway. Walk the impressive 5.7km fortress walls surrounding the old city. Visit Hwaseong Haenggung Palace within the fortress grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's traditional market area near the fortress. Visit the Korean Folk Village (Minsokchon) nearby for an immersive living museum experience showcasing traditional Korean village life, crafts, and performances.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul/Incheon area. Enjoy a relaxed evening near the hotel in Bupyeong — explore the local dining scene or visit a jjimjilbang (Korean sauna/spa) for a premium relaxation experience after a day of walking.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departing for Suwon
meals.lunch: Suwon galbi (Suwon-style short ribs) — a regional specialty that Suwon is famous for. Try Yeonpo Galbi or a similar well-regarded local restaurant near the fortress
meals.dinner: Premium jjimjilbang dinner or a quality Korean restaurant near Bupyeong station — try a local sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) restaurant for warming winter comfort food

day_by_day.notes: Suwon is easily accessible from Bupyeong via subway (Line 1 toward Suwon, approx. 30–40 min). Hwaseong Fortress is beautiful in winter with snow-dusted walls. Wear very warm footwear for the fortress wall walk.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks in Jamsil. Enjoy the festive Christmas Eve decorations and atmosphere. The indoor section is perfect for cold December weather.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the adjacent Lotte World Mall and Lotte World Tower (the 5th tallest building in the world). Visit the Seoul Sky observation deck on the 117th–123rd floors for breathtaking panoramic views of Seoul on a clear winter day.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate Christmas Eve in style. Head to Myeongdong or Cheongdam-dong for the festive Christmas atmosphere. Seoul goes all-out for Christmas Eve with lights, decorations, and events throughout the city.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at one of Lotte World Mall's upscale restaurants — the mall has an excellent food hall with both Korean and international options
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner at a premium restaurant — consider Pierre Gagnaire à Séoul at Lotte Hotel, or a luxury hotel restaurant offering a special Christmas Eve menu. Alternatively, a premium Korean BBQ celebration dinner

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the biggest date nights in Korea — restaurants will be extremely busy. Book dinner reservations at least 1–2 weeks in advance. Seoul Sky tickets can be purchased online to skip queues. Lotte World may have special Christmas Eve events.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning at leisure. Enjoy a premium hotel breakfast. Take a peaceful morning walk along the Han River — Yeouido Hangang Park is beautiful in winter and less crowded on Christmas morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bukhansan National Park for a scenic winter hike — the mountain peaks surrounding Seoul offer stunning views and are accessible by subway. Choose a beginner-friendly trail such as the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail. The snow-dusted mountain scenery is spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas evening celebration in Cheongdam-dong (Seoul's most upscale district). Browse luxury boutiques along Cheongdam-dong's 'Rodeo Drive' — Chanel, Dior, Louis Vuitton flagship stores. Enjoy the premium atmosphere of Seoul's most exclusive neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent hotel breakfast — treat yourself on Christmas morning
meals.lunch: Warm mountain food after the hike — doenjang jjigae (fermented soybean paste stew) or sundubu jjigae at a traditional restaurant near Bukhansan
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner at Dosa in Cheongdam-dong or a premium Korean fine dining restaurant — alternatively, a luxury hotel Christmas dinner buffet at Grand Hyatt Seoul or Shilla Hotel

day_by_day.notes: Many shops and some restaurants may have reduced hours on Christmas Day. Bukhansan National Park is open year-round — trails can be icy, so bring hiking poles and wear appropriate footwear. The park is accessible from Gupabal or Dobongsan subway stations.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea in Yongsan — a powerful and moving museum documenting Korean history and the Korean War. The outdoor exhibits include tanks, aircraft, and artillery. Free admission.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the trendy Seongsu-dong neighborhood — Seoul's 'Brooklyn,' known for its converted industrial spaces, artisan cafés, and creative boutiques. Visit the Daelim Warehouse (a converted factory turned cultural space) and browse independent design shops.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Seoul — return to Hongdae or Gangnam for a farewell celebration. Visit a premium norebang (private karaoke room) for a quintessential Korean entertainment experience — book a luxury suite norebang for the full premium experience.

meals.breakfast: Artisan café breakfast near the hotel or en route
meals.lunch: Trendy brunch at a popular Seongsu-dong café-restaurant — the neighborhood is famous for its specialty coffee and creative food concepts
meals.dinner: Farewell premium Korean BBQ dinner — Hanwoo Grill at a top-tier restaurant such as Cote Korean Steakhouse concept, or a premium samgyeopsal (pork belly) experience at a high-end establishment

day_by_day.notes: Seongsu-dong is best explored on weekends when pop-up markets and events are active. Premium norebang rooms (luxury karaoke suites) can be booked at venues like Su Norebang in Gangnam — a far cry from standard karaoke, with premium sound systems and service.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Incheon/Seoul area. Enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center or a nearby department store. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time — if afternoon/evening departure, visit a nearby jjimjilbang (Korean spa) for a final relaxation session, or explore any remaining items on your Seoul wish list. Head to Incheon Airport with ample time (allow 2–3 hours before international departure).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Enjoy the world-class airport facilities — Incheon Airport has premium lounges, duty-free shopping, and excellent dining options airside.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy Korean staples one last time: doenjang jjigae, rice, banchan (side dishes)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel or at Incheon Airport — the airport has excellent Korean food options including premium restaurants airside
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time carefully and plan hotel checkout accordingly. Incheon Airport is approximately 20–30 minutes from Bupyeong by AREX (Airport Railroad Express) or taxi. Allow extra time for luggage and check-in on busy post-Christmas travel days. Keep some Korean Won for last-minute purchases — airport exchange rates are less favorable.

query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX
